groups.measured: EXHAUSTED the 35 min of the Go `-timeout` inside modules-rest: 2,100 s measured. Its own job for the SAME measurement as finops and governance — not for size, but because it consumes the whole clock of its shard and drags along everything that shares the job. ⇒ CURE: `-parallel 8`. The package did not hang: it did not fit. 799 tests, 730 with t.Parallel(), and only TWO slots on the runner (GOMAXPROCS = the cgroup quota). 403 queued × ~6.5 s ÷ 2 = ~22 min, which are the 23 of the dump. The two tests seen running had been in for 1 s and 25 s: they were FINE. — RE-MEASURED 2026-09-16 (hosted 4 vCPU, race-full 35136307725, 80/70): BOTH halves exhausted the 70 min of Go (a: 379 of 631 top-level tests done, 225 min of test time in 70 of wall clock; b: 421 of 614, 266 min). It did not hang: it did not fit. Eight shards by prefix families, assigned by the model wall = sequential + parallel/P with P=7.4 calibrated on those two halves (-parallel 8): ~27 min estimated per shard, 2.6x below the -timeout. The planner that assigns these shards stays outside the published tree. — RE-MEASURED 2026-10-31 (hosted 4 vCPU, race-full of the 0.5 candidate export, -parallel 8): shards a, c and d were cut at the 70 min -timeout and b and f took 68-70 min of Go time; the package grew since 0.4 (slowest shard 69 min then). Per-test costs of that run fit wall = sequential + parallel/7.4 within 1.5 min on the seven complete shards (3342 top-level tests; cut tests at their elapsed lower bound, never-started ones at the parallel p90). 19 shards keep every predicted job, including 3.4 min of measured start-up, at or under 45 min (slowest 44.8).

measured_run.note: Durations of the `race this group` STEP, read with scripts/race-full-report.sh. modules-rest died at its ceiling (45.2 min of 45) and was split for that reason. ⛔ The provenance is cited WITHOUT repository or run id: this file SHIPS in the published tree, and a private repository name there is a leak — the export's leak gate stopped it, not a review. ⛔ And modules-sessions later moved to its own job: it exhausted the 35 min `-timeout` inside modules-rest (2,100 s). Its figure here is the CEILING it consumed, not its real duration — the real one is unknown because the clock cut it, and that is why it cannot be used for balancing yet.

parallel_why: ⛔ `go test`'s `-parallel` inherits GOMAXPROCS, and since Go 1.25 GOMAXPROCS comes from the cgroup QUOTA, not from the visible CPUs. Measured on one development host: NumCPU 16, quota 6, GOMAXPROCS 6 — and the dump showed EXACTLY 6 parent tests running. On the runner TWO were running, so its effective quota is 2, not the advertised 4 vCPU. With 730 tests that call t.Parallel() and wait on timers and I/O, two slots turn a package of minutes into one that does not fit in 35. `parallel` decouples TEST concurrency from the CPU quota, which is the right thing when what the tests wait for is not CPU. 0 = do not pass the flag.
